speaker_role: independent counselor (self-described educator, Carolyn J Smith)
commercial_incentive: yes -- promotes her own essay-writing course (discounted) at the end
key_insights: Clarifies deferral only applies to early action/early decision applicants whose files are pushed into the regular decision pool for reconsideration, while waitlisting only applies to regular decision applicants
If deferred, recommends following the deferral letter's specific instructions exactly, since some schools explicitly ask applicants not to submit extra materials

Recommends writing a letter of continued interest that is positive, states commitment to attending if admitted, includes transcript/accomplishment updates, and is sent to both the regional admissions officer and copied to the dean of admissions (plus a hard copy to both)
For deferred students, recommends revisiting and restructuring the school list to mentally prepare a 'plan B' in case deferral becomes rejection
For waitlisted students, recommends first securing a deposit at an already-admitted school to reduce stress before deciding whether to pursue the waitlist further
Recommends finding out the size of the waitlist and how many students are typically admitted from it in past cycles to calibrate realistic odds
Advises against letting senior-year grades slide while deferred or waitlisted, as a sign of continued commitment
notable_or_distinctive: Provides a specific, step-by-step protocol for a letter of continued interest (who to send it to, copying the dean, sending both email and hard copy) rather than just saying 'express continued interest.'
reliability_notes: General good-practice advice from an independent educator without citing specific school data or an admissions-office source; the letter-of-continued-interest protocol described (hard copy plus copying the dean) may not match every school's stated preferences.
